attacker.model: claude (Kiro subagent; exact model version not exposed to the agent)

null-vs-empty.notApplicableReason: Every column of Warehouse.StockItemHoldings that the procedure reads is NOT NULL, including BinLocation, so no NULL text value can be sent. '' and ' ' are sent as bin locations in the text case.

cases.label: rows inserted in descending key order, keys at the int limits and with gaps: listed by StockItemID ascending; reorder and target levels differ on every row
cases.reasoning: Ids 2147483647, 1000, 0, -1, -2147483648 are inserted in that order. ORDER BY sih.StockItemID must sort negatives first; a result in insertion order or descending would differ. ReorderLevel and TargetStockLevel differ on every row so a swapped pair shows.

cases.label: LastCostPrice ending in 5 and at 15 significant digits: 0.05, -0.15, 9999999999999.95, -9999999999999.95, 0.00
cases.reasoning: decimal(18,2) is passed through. A conversion through float or money, or a column mapped to numeric with a smaller scale, would change 0.05 / -0.15 (not exact in binary) or the 15-digit values.

cases.label: bin locations as stored: case-only variants, trailing spaces, '' and a single space, ten emoji (20 UTF-16 code units)
cases.reasoning: BinLocation is passed through. 'a-1', 'A-1' and 'A-1 ' are three rows under CI_AS and must keep their spelling; '' and ' ' are different values on output (nvarchar keeps the space). Ten emoji fill nvarchar(20) exactly in UTF-16 code units (10 characters in varchar(20)).

cases.label: quantities at the int limits; equal QuantityOnHand and LastStocktakeQuantity on several rows; ReorderLevel greater than TargetStockLevel
cases.reasoning: QuantityOnHand 2147483647 and -2147483648; three rows share QuantityOnHand 0 and LastStocktakeQuantity 0, ordered only by StockItemID. ReorderLevel 100 > TargetStockLevel 10 on one row.

top-ties.detail: two rows of Warehouse.StockItemHoldings share QuantityOnHand = 0

cases.label: empty table: no rows
cases.reasoning: With no holdings the procedure returns an empty result set with its seven columns. A conversion that aggregated or LEFT JOINed to a driving row would return one row of NULLs.

objections.text: A01 supplies distinct StockItemID values in descending insertion order and therefore would expose the planted descending-order defect under the required ordered comparison. The adversarial plain-SQL assertions compare these rows as a multiset, despite spec.orderKey naming 'WWI Stock Item ID', so no input-only revision can catch the defect. Descending order is observable because the source query guarantees ascending order; it must not be recorded as equivalent. The harness needs to enforce the order key in adversarial assertions.
